evidence.claim: The CLI has two interactive stream sources: legacy Gemini stream and the AgentProtocol-backed stream, selected by getAgentSessionInteractiveEnabled() at mount time.
The CLI has two non-interactive stream sources: runNonInteractive (legacy) and runNonInteractiveAgentSession, selected by getAgentSessionNoninteractiveEnabled() before the prompt loop starts.

LegacyAgentSession adapts the existing Gemini client and scheduler loop to the AgentProtocol interface using an event translator; the same adapter is used by both interactive and non-interactive agent-session drivers.
AgentRegistry discovers and loads built-in, user-level, project-level, and extension-provided agents in that order.
LocalSubagentInvocation executes local agents using LocalAgentExecutor and bridges their streaming activity to the tool's output.
RemoteAgentInvocation bypasses the local executor loop and directly invokes remote A2A agents via A2AClientManager.
Agent scheduling uses a subagent-specific context, including isolated ToolRegistry and PromptRegistry instances.

contradictions.description: Pollux spec/forensic assume a single interceptor between GeminiClient and Turn is sufficient; only two of four drivers (interactive legacy, non-interactive legacy) flow through GeminiClient.sendMessageStream. Both agent-session drivers route through LegacyAgentSession + LegacyAgentProtocol, and ACP bypasses the client entirely.

risks.description: LegacyAgentSession is a temporary adapter and may diverge from pure AgentProtocol semantics over time; Pollux behavior parity across legacy vs agent-session drivers is not test-enforced.
risks.suggestedGuard: assert every new Pollux event round-trips through both adapters

risks.description: Remote invocation relies on network stability and A2A auth and can fail mid-stream.
risks.suggestedGuard: retry/fallback path gated by ModelAvailabilityService snapshot

risks.description: Subagent tool registries are isolated, but concurrent subagents against the same workspace resource can still contend.
AppContainer.tsx:1186-1216 disables rules-of-hooks to switch between useAgentStream and useGeminiStream; if the feature flag flips mid-session, React state corrupts.
risks.suggestedGuard: forbid runtime flag changes and verify in CLI startup

gaps: No test asserts Pollux-event parity across the four drivers (R-03.1).
No test guards against mid-session flip of agent-session flag (R-03.4).

openQuestions: OQ-03.1: When will LegacyAgentSession be fully deprecated in favor of a native AgentSession implementation? Escalate to compartment 02.

OQ-03.2: Does a Pollux interceptor attached at GeminiClient reach the agent-session drivers via LegacyAgentSession's internal use of the client, or must it be re-attached per driver? Escalate to compartment 02.
